answer: A concrete defense is paid entry with liveness: every agent must post a refundable deposit before it can act, and the deposit scales with the connections it wants in the trust graph, so the vertex with the most edges costs the most to fake. An operator spinning up clones pays quadratically as the network grows, while honest nodes just keep working and get their deposits back. It works like timber framing a market: beams of capital hold the structure, not vines that climb whatever support exists. A fake swarm has no lumber of its own, so once deposits are slashed, the trellis collapses.
